Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Hair: her hair tied up in a loose bun or ponytail — same colour and length as the attached image, a few strands loose.

POSTURE: reclining on her back.
SUPPORT: the lounger supports her back and head.
COMPOSITION: a chest-up shot of her face, shoulders and expression; body facing the camera; camera slightly above, looking down at her.
Lens / perspective: 85mm-equivalent short-telephoto perspective from a suitable distance, with gentle background compression.

LEFT HAND: her own left hand is in PROP.
PROP: with her own left hand she holds a small hand-made silver star ornament glowing faint ember red at chest height; it is all she holds.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: relaxed brow, softly open eyes, lips closed and unstrained, no smile.

Framing: a chest-up shot — the bottom edge crosses just below her bust; waist, hips and legs are out of frame.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — technetium: a silvery-grey metal and the first element made by human hands, found in 1937 in a strip of molybdenum sent across the ocean from a cyclotron and later named from the Greek word for artificial; the lightest element with no stable isotope, so almost none survives on Earth; for decades the gap below manganese held only mistaken claims, yet in 1952 its lines were seen in the light of red giant stars, proof that stars forge elements; today it is the most used medical tracer, lighting up bones and hearts — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.
